metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness emits explicit turn boundaries, assistant usage, and a stable session header; the DSH adapter maps all basic-turn observables.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 supports a normal persisted turn in its TUI profile. The installed CLI documentation defines `dsh --profile <name>` and identifies the current directory as the workspace root. A measured local v3 transcript from the installed binary contains the full text-only sequence: `turn/start`, a user message, `request/context` with model `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`, an `assistant/message` with non-zero `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, and `totalTokens`, then `turn/end` with `reason.kind=completed`. This is direct evidence for the agent behavior and durable emission.

The DSH adapter watches `session.vN.jsonl.zstd` under the DSH sessions root. It derives one stable session ID from the parent `session-<uuid>` directory. The parser maps `turn/start` to `turn_start`, the real user record to `user_message`, and completed `turn/end` to `turn_done`. These records produce the required `ready -> working -> ready` arc. The parser maps assistant usage to a token snapshot and a per-turn contribution. It also maps `request/context.model`, so offline replay can verify the exact model and non-zero token count. The compressed-transcript end-to-end parser test covers this combined lifecycle and usage path. The daemon verdict is provisional only for live watcher timing; the measured transcript and parser code cover every required observable.

The interactive driver implements `send`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`. It launches the installed TUI profile with a per-run LM Studio patch, resolves the new durable transcript by marker and cwd, and waits for the expected count of completed `turn/end` records. The recipe matches the sibling settle delay with an 8-second sleep because that delay covers the daemon observation window. The 180-second turn budget covers the measured local model latency.

The model is pinned because the recipe itself sets `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`, and the measured transcript confirms that exact value. Token usage is pinned non-zero. Cost is not pinned non-zero because the recording uses a local LM Studio endpoint and the current irrlicht LiteLLM cache has no exact pricing entry for `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`.
caveats: Vacuous-pass check: the lifecycle and token assertions could pass if the model unexpectedly made an auto-approved tool call and still completed, because the phase invariant language does not reject function-call events. The exact-word prompt minimizes this risk, and recording review must confirm that the curated events contain no tool call.

Load-bearing environment precondition: LM Studio must be listening at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 with qwen/qwen3.5-9b loaded. The driver pins this endpoint and model through its temporary patch; another model would invalidate the exact model assertion.
Load-bearing isolation precondition: the driver must use its fresh per-run cwd and pre-launch marker. This prevents an unrelated DSH transcript from satisfying the single-session phase chain.

The single-birth ready shape and timing bound are inferred from the session header being persisted at TUI launch before the first turn and from FilesUnderRoot session identity. A live irrlichd recording must settle the timing.

sources.note: Installed 0.1.5-rc.2 CLI documentation: named profiles, TUI resume example, persisted headless sessions, and cwd as the workspace root.
Measured v3 transcript: stable session header, one turn/start, text-only assistant reply from qwen/qwen3.5-9b with 7913 input and 25 output tokens, and completed turn/end.
FilesUnderRoot source over compressed DSH transcripts and session.lock-based PID binding.
Maps turn/start, user/message, assistant/message usage and model, request/context, and turn/end to the lifecycle and metric fields required by this cell.
TestParserMapsMeasuredTurnStart, TestParserMapsAssistantUsage, TestParserMapsTurnEnd, and TestZstdTranscriptEndToEnd pin the relevant measured v3 records.
Declares and implements send, wait_turn, and sleep; resolves only readable post-marker transcripts for the run cwd and waits on completed turn/end records.

preconditions: dsh >=0.1.5-rc.2 is installed and on PATH
the community TUI profile is installed under ~/.dsh/profiles/tui
LM Studio is listening at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 with qwen/qwen3.5-9b loaded
irrlichd is recording the deepseek-harness adapter
setup: The interactive driver creates a fresh cwd under the staging directory and launches `dsh --profile tui` in tmux.
The driver applies a temporary patch that selects LM Studio and qwen/qwen3.5-9b without modifying the installed TUI profile.
The driver resolves the new session.v3.jsonl.zstd by pre-launch marker, header cwd, and parent session ID, then waits for the expected completed turn/end count.

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl contains one DSH session born in ready from the post-marker transcript
the same session enters working after the real user message
completed turn/end returns the same session to ready without a waiting transition
the replay summary reports model qwen/qwen3.5-9b and non-zero cumulative tokens
the curated event stream contains no function call for the exact-word prompt
recipe.scope_note: Uses the sibling 8-second post-turn settle delay. DSH emits an explicit completed turn/end, but the daemon still needs an observation window before driver teardown.
